title: Asian Markets Surge on AI Optimism, Even as Iran Tensions Loom【AP News】
body:
Global equity markets displayed a split personality on Thursday, with Asian bourses rallying on the back of renewed enthusiasm for artificial‑intelligence‑driven stocks, while European indices slipped amid lingering concerns over the escalating conflict in Iran. The divergent moves highlighted how investors are simultaneously chasing high‑growth technology themes and weighing geopolitical risk in their portfolio decisions.

In Japan’s Nikkei 225, the index closed up 1.1% after a series of strong earnings reports from leading chipmakers and a surge in AI‑related shares such as SoftBank Group and Sony. South Korea’s KOSPI mirrored the sentiment, gaining 1.3% on the back of a rally in Samsung Electronics and a host of smaller firms that have announced partnerships with major AI developers. The optimism was underpinned by a broader “AI boom” narrative that has been sweeping through the technology sector, with venture capital inflows and corporate spending on generative‑AI tools hitting record levels in recent weeks.

Across the continent, the mood was more cautious. France’s CAC 40 fell 1.8% in early trading, dragged down by heavyweights in the energy and financial sectors that are sensitive to geopolitical developments. Germany’s DAX slipped 1.5%, while Britain’s FTSE 100 lost 1.2%, reflecting a broader risk‑off tone among European investors. Analysts point to the ongoing war in Iran as the primary driver of the downturn, noting that heightened tensions could disrupt oil supplies, trigger sanctions, and dampen investor confidence in markets that are already grappling with inflationary pressures.

The Iranian conflict has resurfaced after a series of missile exchanges between Tehran and Israeli forces, raising the specter of a wider regional escalation. Energy traders have already reported a modest uptick in crude oil prices, which, while still below the peaks seen earlier in the year, have added a layer of uncertainty for industries dependent on stable energy costs. Moreover, the prospect of renewed sanctions on Iranian oil could affect global supply chains, prompting investors to adopt a more defensive stance, especially in Europe where exposure to energy imports is comparatively higher.

In contrast, the AI narrative appears to be gaining momentum as a counterbalance to geopolitical risk. Companies that provide cloud infrastructure, semiconductor manufacturing, and AI software platforms are seeing their valuations buoyed by expectations of a new wave of productivity gains and cost efficiencies. Investment banks have upgraded several AI‑centric stocks, citing robust demand from both enterprise and consumer segments. This sectoral optimism is also reflected in the flow of capital, with several Asian fund managers reallocating assets from traditional heavy industries to technology funds that focus on AI development and deployment.

Nevertheless, market participants remain wary of the sustainability of the AI rally. Critics argue that the hype surrounding generative‑AI could lead to overvaluation, especially if corporate earnings fail to keep pace with lofty expectations. Additionally, regulatory scrutiny on data privacy and AI ethics is intensifying in both the United States and Europe, potentially introducing new compliance costs for firms operating in this space.

Looking ahead, investors will be closely watching how the Iranian situation evolves and whether diplomatic channels can de‑escalate the conflict. A resolution could restore confidence in European markets, while any further escalation might push risk‑averse capital toward safe‑haven assets and technology stocks that are perceived as less vulnerable to geopolitical shocks. Meanwhile, the AI sector is likely to remain a focal point for growth‑oriented investors, provided that companies can translate the current excitement into tangible revenue streams. The coming weeks will test whether the current market bifurcation can endure, or if one narrative will ultimately dominate the global equity landscape.
